title: Sold Six Times Before Samarkand: How the Silk Road Really Worked
title_zh: 在抵达撒马尔罕之前已被转手六次：丝绸之路真实的运作方式
intro_zh: 本文约 564 词，从“商队接力贸易”的角度讲丝绸之路上的具体贸易故事：什么样的货物才经得起长途运输、丝绢如何当钱用、粟特商人如何经营家族商号、玻璃为何易碎、纸张如何西传，以及契约与信任如何替代银行。含 6 个 CET-4 核心词，句子难度中等。

paragraphs.en: The Silk Road was never one road. It was a loose network of paths stretching about 6,400 kilometres from China to the Mediterranean, and almost nobody travelled the whole way. A merchant from Chang'an might sell his goods in Dunhuang; another trader carried them west to Samarkand. Each handover added a little to the price. That one fact explains a lot: the Silk Road was less a long journey than a chain of short, careful bargains.
paragraphs.zh: 丝绸之路从来不是一条路。它是一张松散的道路网，从中国一直延伸到地中海，总长约 6400 公里，而几乎没有人走完全程。长安的商人可能把货卖在敦煌，另一位商人再把它们往西运到撒马尔罕。每一次转手都会让价格往上加一点。这一个事实就能说明很多：与其说丝绸之路是一趟长途旅行，不如说它是一连串短途而谨慎的讨价还价。

paragraphs.en: Not every product survived such a journey. Traders quickly learned that the best goods were light, valuable and hard to break — what we now call luxury items. Silk was perfect: a small roll could be folded, carried on a camel and sold for many times its cost. Spices, gems and perfumes had the same advantage. Grain, by contrast, was heavy and cheap; nobody carried it three thousand kilometres.
paragraphs.zh: 并不是每种商品都能经受这样的旅程。商人们很快明白，最好的货物要轻、值钱、不易损坏——也就是我们今天说的奢侈品。丝绸堪称完美：一小卷可以折叠、放在骆驼背上，卖出好几倍的价钱。香料、宝石和香水也有同样的优势。相反，粮食又重又便宜，没人会把它运上三千公里。

paragraphs.en: Goods moved in caravans. A single camel could carry about 150 to 200 kilos, so a large caravan of 100 animals carried perhaps 18 tonnes — serious business, but slow: 25 to 30 kilometres a day at most. Water, weather and robbers were constant worries. Travellers joined together partly for safety and partly to share the cost of guides and guards.
paragraphs.zh: 货物靠商队运输。一头骆驼大约能驮 150 到 200 公斤，所以一支由 100 头骆驼组成的大商队也许能运 18 吨货——生意不小，但速度很慢：一天最多走 25 到 30 公里。水、天气和强盗是长久的忧虑。旅人们结伴同行，一半是为了安全，一半是为了分摊向导和护卫的费用。

paragraphs.en: Silk was more than cloth. In Tang dynasty China it worked as money. Soldiers on the frontier were sometimes paid in rolls of silk, and taxes could be collected in cloth. Officials treated a standard length as a unit of value, much as we use a banknote. So silk travelled far: even a trader who did not want cloth could use it to pay a guard, buy a meal or settle a debt.
paragraphs.zh: 丝绸不只是布。在唐代中国，它能当钱用。边关士兵有时用成卷的丝绸发饷，税也可以用布匹来缴。官员把一标准长度的丝绢当作价值单位，很像我们今天用纸币。所以丝绸能走得那么远：即使一个并不想要布料的商人，也能用它付护卫的钱、买一顿饭或者还一笔债。

paragraphs.en: The real professionals were neither Chinese nor Roman, but Sogdians from Central Asia. These merchants spoke several languages, kept family firms in many cities and knew which market wanted which goods. A Sogdian trader might send his nephew to Dunhuang and his brother to Persia, then compare prices by letter. Long before modern companies existed, they had built a network that ran on family trust.
paragraphs.zh: 真正的行家既不是中国人也不是罗马人，而是来自中亚的粟特人。这些商人会讲好几种语言，在许多城市开设家族商号，清楚哪个市场需要哪种货。一位粟特商人可能把侄子派到敦煌、把兄弟派到波斯，然后通过书信比较两地的价格。早在现代公司出现之前，他们已经建起了一个靠家族信任运转的网络。

paragraphs.en: Other goods were fragile. Roman and Persian glass travelled east in huge demand, yet broken glass was worthless. Excavations along the route in China have turned up glass fragments, a hint of how much was lost on the way. Chinese porcelain faced the same risk later on sea routes; packers solved it with straw, wooden crates and careful stacking.
paragraphs.zh: 还有些货物是易碎的。罗马和波斯的玻璃需求旺盛、一路东运，但碎玻璃一文不值。中国境内沿线的考古发掘出土过玻璃残片，这暗示了路上损耗了多少。后来中国瓷器在海路上也面临同样的风险；包装者用稻草、木箱和精心堆叠解决了这个问题。

paragraphs.en: Trade also flowed west. Chinese armies wanted horses from Central Asia, and buyers paid for them with silk and tea. In the other direction, paper-making travelled: after papermakers were taken to Samarkand in the eighth century, the skill slowly reached Europe. Few exports ever proved more useful than that quiet bundle of sheets.
paragraphs.zh: 贸易也向西流动。中国军队需要中亚的马匹，买家就用丝绸和茶叶付款。反方向上，造纸术也在传播：公元八世纪造纸工匠被带到撒马尔罕之后，这门手艺慢慢传到了欧洲。很少有哪种输出品比那一捆安静的纸页更有用。

paragraphs.en: Business across such remote distances needed trust, since no merchant could check every partner himself. Written contracts, letters of credit and shared religious communities filled the gap. Documents found at Dunhuang record loans, partnerships and complaints about late payments — small human dramas that sound surprisingly modern.
paragraphs.zh: 跨越如此遥远的距离做生意需要信任，因为没有商人能亲自核查每一个伙伴。书面契约、信用票据和共同的宗教社群填补了这一空缺。敦煌出土的文书里记载着借贷、合伙以及对拖欠付款的抱怨——这些小小的人间戏剧听起来出人意料地现代。

paragraphs.en: The Silk Road's most valuable exports may have been ordinary things: recipes, songs, paper and the habit of dealing with strangers. Its prosperity came not from one great treasure but from thousands of small, patient deals. Today freight trains cover the same ground in about fifteen days instead of a year, yet the basic idea — that people far apart do better by trading than by fighting — has not changed at all.
paragraphs.zh: 丝绸之路最有价值的输出品也许是些寻常之物：食谱、歌曲、纸张，以及同陌生人打交道的习惯。它的繁荣并非来自某一件稀世珍宝，而是来自成千上万笔耐心的小生意。今天货运列车用大约十五天而不是一年就能走完同样的路程，但那个基本的想法——相距遥远的人们做买卖比打仗更划算——一点也没有改变。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How trade along the Silk Road actually worked through short relays of goods and trust.
The personal life story of one Sogdian merchant family.
Why grain was a better trading product than silk.
The invention and spread of the modern freight train.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文围绕“丝绸之路不是一条路，而是短途接力、货物多次转手”的运作方式展开，并涉及货物选择、丝绢当钱、商人网络、契约信任等，A 概括最全面。B 只是第五段的一个细节；C 与第二段相反；D 只在末段作为对照出现。

questions.q: According to the passage, silk was especially suitable for long-distance trade partly because ______.
options: it was heavy, cheap and easy to produce in large amounts
it could be folded and carried easily and could even be used to pay debts
it was the only product that Roman buyers were allowed to purchase
it never broke and could be eaten during the journey
questions.explain: 细节题。第二段说丝绸轻、值钱、可折叠、能用骆驼运；第四段补充说丝绢在唐代可当钱用，能付护卫、买饭、还债。B 与原文一致。A、C、D 均属编造。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the last two paragraphs about written contracts?
options: They were used only by Chinese officials collecting taxes.
They helped traders do business with partners they could not check in person.
They made camel caravans unnecessary on the route.
They were invented after the railway reached Central Asia.
questions.explain: 推理题。倒数第二段说，因为路途遥远、商人无法亲自核查每个伙伴，书面契约和信用票据“填补了这一空缺”，可推知它们帮助商人建立跨距离的信任，故选 B。A 缩小范围；C、D 与原文无关。

questions.q: The word "fragile" in the sixth paragraph is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。该段举罗马和波斯玻璃为例，说“碎玻璃一文不值”，并提到出土玻璃残片，说明这类货物“易碎”，fragile 意为“易碎的、脆弱的”，故选 A。B、C、D 都不符合上下文。
